Not necessarily. Satellite data show about 0.7 ha of tree-cover loss in 2023 (1.2% of the 58.1 ha property). That loss is corroborated: later years were observed, and the 2020 JRC map agrees the area was forest.

However, that does not show deforestation. According to the 2021 national forest map, none of the affected area was native forest. About 0.4 ha was planted eucalyptus, and 0.3 ha was outside mapped forest. Hansen loss includes any stand replacement, such as harvesting a plantation, so this may be routine plantation harvest rather than clearing.

The evidence does not establish:
- whether land use changed
- the cause (harvest, fire, storm, clearing)
- whether it was legal or authorized
- who is responsible
- any compliance finding (e.g., EUDR)

Another ~0.4 ha of loss in patches under 0.5 ha was detected but not counted as an event.
